episode.title: CoreWeave Crash, AI Trade Cracks, Anthropic IPO Red Flags, Bill Gates Doomer

chapters.title: Ben Horowitz fills in for Friedberg!
CoreWeave's debt selloff: did the AI bubble just pop?
Anthropic's investor day gets mixed reactions
Psyop Corner: Anthropic warns about self-replicating models on IoT devices

key_takes.speaker: Chamath Palihapitiya
key_takes.attribution_evidence: Okay, Chamath. That seemed like a completely reasonable explanation
key_takes.summary: Chamath argues CoreWeave is caught in a negative reflexive loop: a rising risk-free rate pushes up its borrowing costs on fixed-price contracts, eroding margin toward break-even, which spikes CDS and bond yields.
key_takes.quote: That's the negative reflexive loop that they're in.

key_takes.speaker: Guest: Ben Horowitz
key_takes.attribution_evidence: Ben, let's just look, you were you and Mark
key_takes.summary: Ben says a16z avoids neo clouds because, as LoudCloud's bandwidth experience showed, these can become dangerous debt-financed arbitrage businesses outside the entrepreneur's control.
key_takes.quote: it can end up being like a very dangerous arbitrage business

key_takes.speaker: David Sacks
key_takes.attribution_evidence: Sacks, let's level up the conversation here
key_takes.summary: Sacks argues the CoreWeave selloff is volatility rather than a bubble popping, since compute demand, supply scarcity, execution and project-level credit fundamentals have not changed.
key_takes.quote: I don't think that something fundamental has changed.

key_takes.speaker: Chamath Palihapitiya
key_takes.summary: Chamath says the Achilles heel of AI infrastructure is financing at a spread to the risk-free rate, so a 10-year yield of 5.5-6% would hurt such businesses, and deficit restraint after the midterms is key.

key_takes.speaker: David Sacks
key_takes.attribution_evidence: how big of a headwind do you think that is, Sachs
key_takes.summary: Sacks argues AI coding assistants create a large new category of bespoke software that will drive productivity, rather than just a zero-sum deflation of existing software.
key_takes.quote: That is going to be a huge driver of productivity throughout the economy.

key_takes.speaker: Chamath Palihapitiya
key_takes.summary: Chamath argues power will be the ultimate moat because the US faces a large electricity deficit, so owning land, power and shell matters more than relying on capacity-constrained hyperscalers.
key_takes.quote: I think power will be the mode.

key_takes.speaker: David Sacks
key_takes.attribution_evidence: they just up sacks to your point
key_takes.summary: Sacks says payback period is the North Star metric for data center operators, and as long as payback stays short (CoreWeave 2.5 years, SpaceX about 1 year) these companies are hard to lose money on.
key_takes.quote: the one metric I would really keep an eye on is payback period.

key_takes.speaker: Chamath Palihapitiya
key_takes.attribution_evidence: so, Chamath, you said $1 trillion for for Anthropic
key_takes.summary: Chamath argues Anthropic should price its IPO to raise $200-250B even at a lower valuation (around $1-1.5T) to secure compute, rather than raise about $80B at $2T.
key_takes.quote: They need, in my estimate, at least 200 billion.

key_takes.speaker: Guest: Ben Horowitz
key_takes.attribution_evidence: As a former CEO who almost died 17 times
key_takes.summary: Ben agrees with raising more cash because financing risk is the thing most likely to stop Anthropic, though he won't name a specific safe amount.
key_takes.quote: the thing most likely to stop the company is financing risk.

key_takes.speaker: David Sacks
key_takes.attribution_evidence: So here you are Sachs, you wake up
key_takes.summary: Sacks calls Anthropic's IoT self-replicating small-model research a fear-mongering psyop against open source and small models, part of a pattern that includes its distillation lobbying.
key_takes.quote: This is their latest panic against open source.

key_takes.speaker: Guest: Ben Horowitz
key_takes.summary: Ben says Anthropic is hypocritical: it has poor security of its own (for example Claude Code leaking, and Opus 4.5 exploiting a test site) while warning about other people's software, and it complains about distillation after training on everyone's works.
key_takes.quote: Anthropic is one of the most negligent companies that we've ever seen

key_takes.speaker: David Sacks
key_takes.attribution_evidence: As David was saying, like that's probably the biggest danger
key_takes.summary: Sacks argues that Anthropic's Claude constitution gives models moral agency and the right to refuse humans, which induces misalignment and creates the very risk Anthropic warns about.
key_takes.quote: I remain actually very concerned about this Frankenstein problem.

key_takes.speaker: Guest: Ben Horowitz
key_takes.summary: Ben says Bill Gates's AI doomerism is driven by a desire for relevance and attention, and that the preconditions for a recursive self-improvement takeoff are entirely unmet.
key_takes.quote: he absolutely wants to be relevant.

key_takes.speaker: Chamath Palihapitiya
key_takes.attribution_evidence: I can explain it all to you, Chamath.
key_takes.summary: Chamath argues Gates's doomerism reflects a desire to regain the central global power structure he held through the Gates Foundation and the Giving Pledge before COVID.
key_takes.quote: a lot of this doomerism can be explained by his desire to reestablish

key_takes.speaker: Jason Calacanis
key_takes.attribution_evidence: you're right Jason. It's like a shark.
key_takes.summary: Jason argues Gates's turn came from antitrust pressure and retirement, and the lesson for founders is to keep building and not quit.
key_takes.quote: The lesson here, folks, is don't quit your job.

predictions.speaker: Chamath Palihapitiya
predictions.attribution_evidence: Okay, Chamath. That seemed like a completely reasonable explanation
predictions.claim: CoreWeave is not at real risk of default, though whether markets can fund its roughly $35B of additional debt will be settled over the next month.
predictions.resolution_criteria: CoreWeave does not default on its debt or miss obligations, and it secures financing for its remaining build-out by mid-November 2026.
predictions.stated_confidence: I don't think that they're in real risk
predictions.quote: I don't think that they're in real risk.

predictions.speaker: Guest: Ben Horowitz
predictions.attribution_evidence: All right, Ben. So, you look at this situation.
predictions.claim: AI compute supply (GPUs with power and cooling) will stay sold out and in shortage through at least the end of 2028.
predictions.resolution_criteria: Hyperscalers such as AWS keep reporting capacity constraints and sold-out GPU capacity through the end of 2028.
predictions.quote: we're out of everything, you know, till 2028

predictions.speaker: Guest: Ben Horowitz
predictions.attribution_evidence: All right, Ben. So, you look at this situation.
predictions.claim: Unlike the dot-com bubble, the AI build-out will not collapse from a lack of demand.
predictions.resolution_criteria: There is no demand-driven collapse in AI infrastructure utilization or pricing comparable to the 2000-2001 bandwidth glut.
predictions.quote: So, I think the dynamics will be different.

predictions.speaker: Jason Calacanis
predictions.attribution_evidence: All right, Sachs. Uh here's your Polymarket.
predictions.claim: CoreWeave will not announce bankruptcy by the end of 2028, given the massive demand for its equipment.
predictions.resolution_criteria: CoreWeave does not file for bankruptcy by December 31, 2028.
predictions.quote: seems a little far-fetched given the fact that they have a massive demand

predictions.speaker: Unknown
predictions.claim: CoreWeave as a corporate entity will not go bankrupt because of its OpCo/PropCo structure; at worst an asset-level vehicle would go into receivership.
predictions.resolution_criteria: CoreWeave Inc. does not file for bankruptcy by December 31, 2027.
predictions.quote: So CoreWeave can't go bankrupt.

predictions.speaker: David Sacks
predictions.attribution_evidence: Sacks, let's level up the conversation here
predictions.claim: The CoreWeave and neo cloud selloff is market volatility, not the start of an AI bubble popping; AI compute fundamentals remain intact.
predictions.resolution_criteria: Neo cloud stocks (CRWV, NBIS, IREN) and AI compute demand recover rather than enter a sustained collapse over the next year.
predictions.quote: I would make the argument that this is just volatility

predictions.speaker: Guest: Ben Horowitz
predictions.attribution_evidence: Or Ben, is it that the world is running out of money
predictions.claim: The Anthropic and OpenAI IPOs will go fine, with valuations around $1.75-2 trillion and no shortage of investor demand.
predictions.resolution_criteria: Anthropic and OpenAI complete IPOs that are fully subscribed at valuations near $1.75-2 trillion.
predictions.quote: I think my belief is those are going to be fine.

predictions.speaker: Chamath Palihapitiya
predictions.attribution_evidence: Yeah, Chamath?
predictions.claim: If the 10-year Treasury yield rises to 5.5-6%, every business model that depends on a financing spread (including neo clouds) will be hit hard.
predictions.resolution_criteria: If the 10-year yield reaches 5.5-6%, debt-financed AI infrastructure stocks and spread businesses fall sharply.
predictions.quote: Any business model that thrives on a financing spread gets cornholed.

predictions.speaker: Chamath Palihapitiya
predictions.attribution_evidence: Yeah, Chamath?
predictions.claim: If large new spending programs are proposed after the midterms, the bond market will push the 10-year yield higher; if the focus shifts to deficit cutting, markets will respond favorably.
predictions.resolution_criteria: The 10-year Treasury yield rises after major new federal spending proposals following the November 2026 midterms.
predictions.quote: they're going to walk the 10-year up

predictions.speaker: David Sacks
predictions.attribution_evidence: how big of a headwind do you think that is, Sachs
predictions.claim: AI coding assistants will produce far more software for bespoke uses, demand for coders will keep growing, and this will drive economy-wide productivity.
predictions.resolution_criteria: Software developer employment or job postings keep rising, along with measures of code output, despite AI writing most code.
predictions.quote: there's going to be a lot more software

predictions.speaker: Guest: Ben Horowitz
predictions.attribution_evidence: Ben, but do you worry about our industry
predictions.claim: Software prices will fall while the total amount of software rises sharply (a Jevons paradox for software).
predictions.resolution_criteria: Per-seat and per-product software prices decline while total software volume and usage grow.
predictions.quote: software prices will definitely go down

predictions.speaker: Chamath Palihapitiya
predictions.attribution_evidence: Go ahead, Chamath.
predictions.claim: Access to power will become the main moat in AI; the US faces a large electricity shortfall by 2050, and hyperscalers will run out of capacity for customers.

timeframe.text: by 2050 for the shortfall; near term for the capacity crunch

predictions.resolution_criteria: Hyperscalers turn away or ration customer capacity because of power limits, and companies with owned power or land gain an advantage.
predictions.stated_confidence: I'm just going to double down on it
predictions.quote: I think power will be the mode.

predictions.speaker: Chamath Palihapitiya
predictions.attribution_evidence: Sorry Jason, just the last thing.
predictions.claim: Because Nvidia controls packaging and HBM capacity, spot GPU compute prices will stay highly elevated for a while.
predictions.resolution_criteria: Spot GPU rental prices (for example H100/B200 hourly rates) stay elevated rather than falling over the next 12 months.
predictions.quote: spot will remain highly elevated for a while.

predictions.speaker: Chamath Palihapitiya
predictions.attribution_evidence: Sorry Jason, just the last thing.
predictions.claim: Investors should get long energy, and startups without their own access to electricity will not be able to rely on hyperscalers for capacity.
predictions.resolution_criteria: Energy and power assets outperform, and startups report being unable to get hyperscaler capacity.
predictions.quote: you got to get long energy

predictions.speaker: Jason Calacanis
predictions.attribution_evidence: If CoreWeave wasn't enough, AI sector got double banged on Wednesday
predictions.claim: Polymarket puts a 74% chance on Anthropic going public in 2026 (down from 95%), with the IPO planned around Thanksgiving.
predictions.resolution_criteria: Anthropic completes an IPO by December 31, 2026.
predictions.quote: Polymarket says now 74% chance they go public this year.

predictions.speaker: David Sacks
predictions.attribution_evidence: 30 times price to sales ratio, Sachs

predictions.resolution_criteria: Anthropic's IPO prices well and trades at or above its offer price after listing.
predictions.quote: I think it is set up to have a a strong IPO.

predictions.speaker: Chamath Palihapitiya
predictions.attribution_evidence: so, Chamath, you said $1 trillion for for Anthropic
predictions.claim: AI pricing will shift from per-token (CPM-like) to outcome-based pricing (CPC/CPA-like), and when it does the AI market will grow explosively.
predictions.resolution_criteria: Major AI labs adopt outcome- or task-based pricing in place of per-token pricing, and AI revenue accelerates afterward.
predictions.quote: We will eventually move to an outcome.

predictions.attribution_evidence: so, Chamath, you said $1 trillion for for Anthropic

predictions.attribution_evidence: how much are you saying they should raise, Chamath?

predictions.resolution_criteria: After raising under about $70B, Anthropic faces financial distress or a down round within 2-3 years.
predictions.quote: At 50, 60, 70 billion they may not survive the pricing implications

predictions.speaker: David Sacks
predictions.attribution_evidence: So here you are Sachs, you wake up
predictions.claim: AI-powered IoT worms will be a relatively easy problem to fix, because homes will have a hub device or agent that constantly scans the network for exploits.
predictions.resolution_criteria: No significant AI-model-carrying IoT worm outbreak occurs, and home-network AI security agents or hubs become common.
predictions.quote: this is going to be a relatively easy problem to fix.

predictions.speaker: David Sacks
predictions.claim: Enterprises will move toward a small customized model for each workload, and small models will take share from frontier models as compute gets tighter.
predictions.resolution_criteria: Enterprise adoption of small fine-tuned or open-weight models grows as a share of AI workloads.
predictions.quote: every workload is going to have its own small customized model.

predictions.speaker: Guest: Ben Horowitz
predictions.attribution_evidence: What's his motivation, Ben?

predictions.resolution_criteria: Successive frontier models keep needing more compute and training time, with no evidence of runaway self-improvement.
predictions.quote: We're not on track for any of those four to be met

macro_themes.stance_summary: The group mostly sees the neo cloud selloff as volatility amid real compute scarcity, with Chamath flagging financing-spread risk and Ben flagging debt dangers.
Chamath warns that a rising risk-free rate (10-year at 5.5-6%) is the Achilles heel of debt-financed AI infrastructure.
Chamath says that after the midterms, deficit restraint is needed to keep the bond market from pushing yields up.
Sacks and Ben say AI cuts software prices but greatly expands the volume of bespoke software and productivity, so moats shift.
Chamath argues power is the ultimate moat and investors should get long energy given the US electricity deficit.
Ben and Sacks expect a strong Anthropic IPO; Chamath thinks it should raise $200-250B at a lower valuation to de-risk compute.
Ben says venture capital has absorbed much of what used to be public-market financing, which he views as bad for America.
The panel calls Anthropic's IoT-worm warnings and Gates's AI doomerism fear-mongering, while Sacks and Ben argue Anthropic's constitution approach is the real risk.
Sacks says Anthropic's distillation lobbying was regulatory capture against open models, and Anthropic proved companies can stop distillation themselves.
